claim: A third of the questions that your customers are actually asking have zero search volume. Not low, but zero.

Finding these missing questions is a big part of the SEO game now because you don't want to rank for a specific keyword now, you want to rank for a topic. The way to become the topical authority figure is answer as many of these questions as you can — that's how you'll get cited and recommended by things like GPT search and Google AI overviews.
Fonti dove le domande sono già scritte: Reddit, tue recensioni e recensioni dei clienti, autocomplete, People Also Ask, fan out queries, e altre.

15 of the 37 questions have zero Google search volume. Every one came from a real customer. — soglia esplicita: il volume zero non è motivo di scarto se la domanda proviene da linguaggio cliente reale.

Questions that are objections become FAQs on the service page that has to overcome them. Questions with real demand become their own page, linked from that FAQ. Questions that need showing rather than telling become videos. Nothing is discarded.

Fan-out query: quando un motore di ricerca AI (Google AI overviews, ChatGPT) riceve una domanda complessa, non la elabora direttamente ma si pone internamente domande correlate successive (fan out queries), nascoste ma recuperabili tramite DataForSEO, per costruire una risposta più completa che possa citarti.

Fan-out: What the engine breaks your question into. Take one mixed question and look at what Google's own AI Overview does with it. The sections it needs are the outline of the piece you should build, and the references tell you who is being cited for it today.

Esempio fan-out: query 'metal roof vs shingle?' scomposta dall'AI Overview in 4 sezioni: 1. Cost & Installation, 2. Lifespan & Durability, 3. Energy Efficiency & Climate, 4. Maintenance & Weight. 'Currently cited': roofmaxx.com, sheffieldmetals.com, nerdwallet.com, reddit.com. '4 sections, so this is article-sized rather than a one-paragraph FAQ.'

Legenda routing 1/4 — 'answered here, FAQ, terminal': A real objection with no standalone demand. Nobody ranks a page for it, but leaving it unanswered costs the job, and a direct question-and-answer pair is what AI engines quote.
Legenda routing 2/4 — 'links to full post, FAQ that links out': An objection that also has demand. A short answer on the service page to unblock the sale, then a link to the full piece.

Legenda routing 3/4 — 'post, Its own page': Upstream research. Earns a page when demand is real, or when the AI Overview splits the answer into two or more sections, which means it cannot be answered in a paragraph.
Legenda routing 4/4 — 'video, Video': The answer is something in your hands, and the live [demonstration] — l'intento di ricerca richiede dimostrazione visiva.
The plan, service page by service page. Left column is what gets added to the page itself. Right column is what gets built and linked from it. Every line carries the evidence that earned it.

What else goes on the service pages: From 941 reviews, unprompted — tabella 'Share of 1-2★ reviews (44)' vs 'Share of 5★ reviews (880)': Price shock/second opinion 4,5%/0,5%; Explained what they were doing 11,4%/14,1%; Turned up when they said they would 0,0%/8,1%; Cleaned up after themselves 4,5%/6,6%; Stood behind the work 15,9%/3,5%; Never called back 0,0%/0,0%; Had to come back and redo it 4,5%/0,8%; Handled the paperwork or claim 34,1%/25,2%.

Attributes nobody was asked about. A wide gap between the two columns is a differentiator worth putting on the page. A narrow gap means it's table stakes and wins you nothing. With only 44 reviews at 1-2 stars, the left column is a small sample and should be read as direction, not precision.

Volume figures are monthly averages. A Google figure of 0 means it wasn't queried, and genuinely zero. n/a means it could not be queried, because Google Ads rejects keywords over ten words.

Lesson 6 | Write Content That AI Loves — 5 rules: 1. use real questions as your H2s and H3s, not generic labels; 2. back every claim with a high-quality source linked from the contextual keyword; 3. add your own experience because that is the one thing AI cannot copy; 4. include one or two tables; 5. internally link to other sections of your site.
Common mistakes to skip: rewriting for the sake of it, chasing an arbitrary word count, and stuffing your prompt with 25 personas. Context beats prompt complexity.

Why it's shaped like this — You're not ranking for a keyword. You're ranking for the topic. The old way: One page, one keyword, optimised hard. Repeat 12 times and hope. What actually works now: Answer every real question in the topic, properly, in their words, and link it together. Google and the AI engines both decide who covers a subject completely.
That's why the output is a connected plan, not a list. The service page can't win the topic on its own.
